text: Shilla Monogram opens first property in Hà Nội

HÀ NỘI - Shilla Monogram Hanoi Westlake, a new flagship property of South Korea's leading hospitality corporation The Shilla Hotels & Resorts, has officially entered operation, marking the brand's debut in the Vietnamese capital.

The 319-room hotel welcomed its first guests on October 23. It is situated at No 6 Hoàng Minh Thảo Street in Hà Nội's Xuân Đỉnh Ward, part of the 186-hectare Starlake urban development to the west of Hồ Tây (West Lake).
The ward is currently being developed into a new administrative, commercial and residential hub for the capital.
The Hà Nội opening represents the fourth Shilla Monogram property globally.

The Shilla Hotels & Resorts first expanded its footprint in Việt Nam with the debut of its maiden Shilla Monogram brand in Đà Nẵng on the central coast in June, 2020, before launching properties in Gangneung in South Korea and Xi'an in China.
Operated under The Shilla's management framework, the brand incorporates regional architectural elements into contemporary hotel design.
In Hà Nội, the building's layered exterior and structural lines draw reference from Việt Nam's terraced rice fields.

Positioned near the diplomatic quarter, foreign embassies and international corporate offices, the hotel connects directly to main arterial routes leading to central Hà Nội and lies about 25 minutes by road from Nội Bài International Airport.
Its location is geared towards business travellers, expatriates, long-stay guests and tourists visiting the capital.
Accommodation comprises 319 guest rooms and suites designed for short-term corporate stays, family trips and extended visits.
Room layouts focus on functional furnishings and standard business and leisure amenities.
Food and beverage operations are divided across five venues covering international and East Asian cuisines.
Dining M serves an international buffet with live cooking stations, while Pastry M provides baked goods, afternoon tea, bingsu and beverages.
HASUNGO focuses on Chinese cuisine, including Peking duck, dim sum and seafood.
On the 35th floor, Bar M and the Monogram Lounge operate alongside an outdoor infinity pool, offering views across West Lake and the city skyline.
A fifth venue, the Korean barbecue restaurant JINJI, is scheduled to open in December and will include private dining rooms.
The property includes a 700-square-metre Grand Ballroom with a maximum capacity of 620 guests for meetings, incentives, conferences and exhibitions.
The ballroom can be partitioned into smaller spaces and links directly to a pre-function foyer, meeting rooms and outdoor areas. - VNS
